title: Sanger Tree of Life HMW DNA Extraction: Manual MagAttract
author: Michelle Strickland

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer Master Mix
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents to create the lysis buffer master mix: 200 µL Phosphate buffered solution (PBS), 20 µL Proteinase K, 4 µL RNase A, and 150 µL Buffer AL.

steps.title: Sample Homogenization
steps.instruction: Process samples based on their preparation method using the lysis buffer master mix.

substeps.instruction: For cryoPREP samples: Transfer 25 mg sample into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube on dry ice. Remove from dry ice, add 374 µL lysis buffer master mix, and homogenize by gently pipetting 10 times with a wide bore pipette tip.

For PowerMashed samples (< 25 mg): Transfer sample into a 1.5 mL BioMasher II tube and add 374 µL lysis buffer. Disrupt using a Diagnocine PowerMasher II tissue disruptor and BioMasher pestle until no large pieces remain. Transfer entire contents to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube using a wide-bore tip.

steps.title: Lysis and Incubation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge sample tubes briefly in a mini-centrifuge, then incubate on a heat block at 25 °C for 2 hours.

steps.title: Post-Lysis Recovery
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge samples in a mini-centrifuge to spin down. Using a wide-bore pipette tip set to 380 µL, transfer the lysate to individual microcentrifuge tubes, avoiding insoluble material.

steps.title: Bead Binding
steps.instruction: Add 280 µL Buffer MB and 15 µL Suspension G beads to each sample. Invert the tube 10–20 times to suspend beads and allow 5 minutes for binding.

steps.title: Bead Collection and Initial Wash
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge samples in a mini-centrifuge. Place tubes on a magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes (longer for viscous samples), then remove and discard the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Add 700 µL Buffer MW1 directly to the bead pellet.
Invert the tube 10–20 times to suspend beads.
Place on magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes for beads to migrate.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Add 700 µL Buffer PE directly to the bead pellet.
Invert 10–20 times to resuspend beads.
Place on magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes for beads to migrate.
Remove and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Residual Buffer Removal
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge tubes in a mini-centrifuge and place back on the magnetic rack. Use a small micropipette to remove any residual wash buffer.

steps.title: Water Wash
steps.instruction: Perform the water wash twice (as per the final instruction in the text).

substeps.instruction: While tubes are on the magnetic rack, pipette 700 µL nuclease-free water onto the side opposite the beads (do not pipette directly onto the pellet).
Incubate for exactly 1 minute.
Slowly aspirate and discard the water.

steps.title: gDNA Elution - First Fraction
steps.instruction: Remove samples from the magnetic rack and add 200 µL Buffer AE directly to the bead pellet.

substeps.instruction: Mix by gently flicking or using a wide-bore pipette tip to dislodge the pellet.
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature, mixing gently halfway through and at the end.
Briefly centrifuge (spin down) in a mini-centrifuge.
Place on a magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes for bead migration.
Using a 200 μL wide-bore pipette tip, transfer the supernatant (purified gDNA) to a fresh microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: gDNA Elution - Second Fraction
steps.instruction: Perform a second elution to maximize recovery.

substeps.instruction: Remove sample from magnetic rack and add 200 μL Buffer AE to the bead pellet.
Incubate on the heat block at 25 °C, shaking at 1,000 rpm for three minutes.
Centrifuge briefly in a mini-centrifuge and place on a magnetic rack for 2–5 minutes for bead migration.
Using a wide-bore pipette tip, transfer the supernatant to the same microcentrifuge tube used in the first elution.

steps.title: Storage
steps.instruction: Store the extracted gDNA sample at 4 °C.
